title: Operational Slate: Company-wide Controls & Templates
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines a compact, company-wide set of controls, operational procedures, and reusable templates for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended to be a single-pane reference for engineering, product, finance, security, and people teams.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved third parties.
- Covers corporate systems, customer-facing services, and internal tooling unless a specific system-level exception exists.

Principles
- Least privilege: Access is granted for the minimum set of permissions required to perform a role.
- Separation of duties: Approval, execution, and audit functions are segregated where practical.
- Auditability: All requests, approvals, and non-trivial changes must be recorded in the canonical systems.
- Risk proportionality: Controls scale with sensitivity and business impact.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose
Provide an auditable, role-oriented approach to granting, reviewing, and revoking access across cloud consoles, internal apps, admin systems, and on-prem resources.

Key roles and responsibilities
- System Owner: Defines required roles and least-privilege permissions for their service.
- Access Requestor: Employee or contractor requesting access.
- Approver: Role owner or manager required for approval (see approval matrix).
- Access Coordinator (IAM team): Executes access grants, logs changes, and schedules reviews.

Standard process (new access)
1. Submit a request using the Access Request template in the Templates section.
2. Requestor provides justification, duration (if temporary), and scope.
3. Service owner or manager reviews and approves in the identity system (IAM ticket).
4. Access Coordinator performs the grant, records the grant ticket ID, and notifies requestor.

Temporary access and emergency escalations
- Temporary access (<= 14 days) can be approved by the service owner with a mandatory expiry timestamp.
- Emergency access (e.g., SEV-level incidents) requires post-facto approval within 48 hours and must include explanation and a rollback plan.

Periodic entitlement reviews
- Quarterly automated entitlement reports are generated by IAM and distributed to service owners. Owners must attest within 10 business days.
- Any un-attested entitlements are reviewed by the security team and may be revoked pending investigation.

Access thresholds (examples)
- Admin-level cloud console access: executive approval + security review.
- Database write access to production: service owner + SRE lead approval.
- Read-only observability access: manager approval.

2) Change Management
Definitions
- Standard change: Low-risk changes that follow an approved runbook (no CAB required).
- Significant change: Changes affecting production behavior, schema migrations, or capacity planning (CAB required).
- Emergency change: Time-sensitive changes to mitigate active incidents.

Change request workflow
1. Create a change ticket in the change management system with: scope, rollback plan, monitoring plan, and scheduled window.
2. Classification: change owner tags the ticket as Standard/Significant/Emergency.
3. For Significant changes, submit to the weekly CAB 72 hours before the window with required artifacts.
4. CAB members: SRE, Security, Service Owner, Product Lead, and an independent reviewer.
5. Post-change validation: owner runs the checklist and records metrics.

Emergency change handling
- Emergency changes must be logged immediately with the ‘emergency’ tag and documented within 24 hours.
- Retrospective review required within 5 business days.

Rollback and safety checks
- All significant changes must include: pre-change backup snapshot ID, automated health checks, and a clearly documented rollback command sequence.

3) Data Management
Classification and handling
- Data classification levels: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED.
- Minimum handling requirements:
  - PUBLIC: no special controls.
  - INTERNAL: logging enabled, TLS in transit.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: encryption at rest, access limited to role list, masking for non-product contexts.
  - RESTRICTED: HSM/KMS-backed encryption, strict access reviews, prohibited export without explicit legal sign-off.

Retention & deletion
- Default retention: product logs 90 days; metrics 365 days; backups 30 days unless longer retention approved by service owner.
- Data deletion requests must follow the Data Deletion Request template and are executed within the agreed SLA (typically 14 days).

Data transfer and third-party processors
- All cross-border data transfers must be documented and approved by Legal.
- Vendors handling RESTRICTED data require a Security Assessment and a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

Encryption and key management
- All sensitive production data must be encrypted at rest using company-managed KMS keys.
- Key rotation: annually or immediately after suspected compromise.

4) Procurement & Expense Policy
Approval matrix (summary)
- <= $2,000: Direct manager approval.
- $2,001 – $25,000: Manager + Finance approver.
- $25,001 – $250,000: Head of function + Finance director.
- > $250,000: Executive sponsor + VP Finance + Legal review.

Procurement process (vendor or capex)
1. Complete Procurement Request template with business justification, budget code, and expected contract term.
2. Procurement team validates budget availability and recommends supplier shortlist.
3. For software subscriptions or cloud spend > $10k/year, include an ops/security impact summary.
4. Legal reviews and signs contracts > $25k or any contract containing data clauses.

Employee expenses (travel & expense reports)
- Employees should use the company expense system and submit receipts within 14 days.
- Per diem / caps: see Travel section below.
- Non-compliant expenses (e.g., personal entertainment not pre-approved) are denied by Finance and will be recovered.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding checklist (essentials)
- Business justification & owner identified.
- Security assessment: at minimum a questionnaire; for high-risk vendors an architecture review.
- Contract template with SLA, termination, and data clauses.
- PO issued and budget tagged.

Risk tiers and controls
- Tier 1 (High risk, e.g., stores RESTRICTED data): Full SOC2 or equivalent, quarterly security reviews, contract with explicit breach obligations.
- Tier 2 (Medium risk): Annual security attestations, contractual SLAs, limited data access.
- Tier 3 (Low risk): Standard procurement terms, no sensitive data access.

Vendor review cadence
- Quarterly health checks for Tier 1, annual review for Tier 2, biennial for Tier 3.

Offboarding and contract closeout
- Revoke all credentials and API keys within 24 hours of termination.
- Validate data return/destruction per contract.
- Capture lessons learned in the Vendor Offboarding form.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Booking & approvals
- All business travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Request template.
- Use the corporate booking portal where available for negotiated rates.

Allowed expenses and limits
- Air travel: economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy allowed for flights > 6 hours with manager approval.
- Hotel: up to $250/night in primary metro areas; manager approval required for higher rates.
- Meals: up to $75 per day; itemized receipts required.

Insurance and emergency assistance
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency repatriation for approved trips.
- For high-risk or travel to restricted countries, contact Security and People Ops at least 14 days before travel.

International travel and visas
- Travelers are responsible for securing required visas; People Ops will reimburse visa fees with receipts.

7) Internal Templates (canonical forms)
All templates are available in the central templates library. Included examples below (snippet).

Access Request template (snippet)
- Requestor: [name]
- System: [service name]
- Role requested: [role]
- Justification: [business reason]
- Duration: [permanent | temporary (end date)]
- Approver: [manager/service owner]

Change Request checklist (snippet)
- Change ID: [auto-generated]
- Owner: [name]
- Type: [Standard|Significant|Emergency]
- Rollback steps: [commands/checklist]
- Health checks: [metrics to validate]

Procurement Request template (snippet)
- Requestor: [name]
- Budget code: [GLXX]
- Supplier: [vendor name]
- Term: [months/years]
- Business justification & expected ROI: [text]

Vendor Onboarding checklist (snippet)
- Vendor name: [name]
- Tier: [1|2|3]
- Data access required: [NONE|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|RESTRICTED]
- Security assessment link: [url]

8) Governance & Review
- Policy owner for this document: Finance & Legal (operational custody), with cross-functional editorial ownership by Security and People Ops.
- Review cadence: annual formal review, quarterly check-ins for critical sections (access, change, data).
- Exceptions: documented exceptions require a written risk acceptance and senior sponsor.
